findings.reason: it redirects the node from "add a publish-side check" to "name why the existing guard misses and repair that owner", which is a different and smaller change.
findings.text: §13's done-when tells the node to make the supervisor's publish "check under its lock that the pointer still exists and the run is not discarded"; `_publish_stored_phase` (dispatch.py:10245) already does exactly this, under `_pointer_lock`, and already calls `_write_existing_pointer` (dispatch.py:5030, docstring: "Write only a live run's pointer, clearing a discard that races the write"). The plan proposes the guard as new instead of citing the one that exists.

findings.reason: the node should reuse §14's helpers rather than describe a second derivation of the same idea, turning the section into an extension of landed machinery.
findings.text: §12 proposes bounding the flaky test's window "from a measured figure" without citing `_measured_reference_seconds` (line 800) and `_dispatch_exit_bound` (line 834), the measured-reference helpers §14 already landed in this same file; the load-sensitive bound is the fixed `run.process.wait(timeout=SPAWN_BOUND)` in `test_dispatch_returns_when_its_supervisor_finished_the_launch`.

findings.reason: the finding names the owner to extend (`_write_existing_pointer`) and the concrete writer that escapes it, so the node repairs one mechanism instead of forking a parallel one.
findings.text: §13's fix would place a second "is this pointer still live" check beside the mechanism that owns it, `_write_existing_pointer` (dispatch.py:5030), which checks both sides of its atomic replacement under the lock precisely so "a discard that races the write" is cleared; the reproduction discards by a bare `pointer.unlink()` + `shutil.rmtree(run_directory)` at tests/test_dispatch_returns_without_worker.py:1235-1236, which takes no pointer lock, unlike the product's `discard` (promotion.py:8727, `with _pointer_lock(run_id)`).

findings.reason: naming `placement.py` as the owner of host placement state lets the author extend it rather than maintain the dotfiles path, and aligns §10's text with the decision already locked on the plan.
findings.text: §10 (plan lines 700-703) keeps a second host-state record, `~/.local/state/fleet/record.json` (`RECORD_NAME`, `STATE_DIR_ENV`, fleet_supervisor.py:78-83), read and written beside `reckon/crew/placement.py`'s reservation record (`reservation_path`, placement.py:86), yet the lead's locked decision recorded on this plan (comment c-20260924T150420460935) is that the fleet record is "folded into reckon's placement record".

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §3's per-run supervisor hides the boundary snapshot, the worker spawn, the wait and the exit collection behind one launch interface, and §10's `fleet_supervisor` hides the FIFO protocol, environment stripping and detached spawn behind one `spawn` line.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §13 prescribes a publish-side existence check that `_write_existing_pointer` already implements, and §10 keeps a second host-state record beside `reckon/crew/placement.py`.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §12 (plan line 1000) prescribes deriving the load-sensitive wait from "a measured figure" but does not cite the measured-reference helpers §14 already landed in the same test file.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the two open sections repair existing mechanisms (§12 a test bound, §13 a pointer write) rather than adding a layer; where a new module does appear (`reckon/crew/supervisor_main.py`) it is a launch entry point whose justification is stated.
